audit_findings.title: About a quarter of the anchor is a FAS/CAS pension recovery that runs off, capitalised to perpetuity
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,518m FAS/CAS pension operating adjustment in 2025 segment-to-consolidated reconciliation ($1,624m 2024, $1,660m 2023); CAS pension cost $1,568m vs FAS service cost $50m; ~$1,286m after-tax at the filed 15.3% 2025 effective rate = 22.8% of the $5,650.9m anchor. Prepayment credits fell $2.2bn to $1.9bn; no required 2026 contribution; 2025 cash contribution $860m, nil in H1 2026.
audit_findings.mechanism: Enters the numerator: segment operating profit is struck on CAS cost, and the +$1,518m FAS/CAS operating adjustment is inside 2025 consolidated operating profit, hence inside anchor OE. The anchor is then grown 2% for ten years and 2.5% in perpetuity, and TV is 49% of BASE, so the item is valued as a growing perpetuity.
audit_findings.evidence: We recovered $1.6 billion in 2025 and $1.7 billion in 2024 as CAS pension costs.
audit_findings.explanation: Demonstrated presence, unresolved durability. The adjustment is filed and is large relative to the anchor; what the record does not establish is how fast it runs off. It is not phantom income — CAS recovery is cash the US Government pays in price, and in 2025 recovery ($1.6bn) exceeded cash contributions ($0.86bn) — but it is the spread between a government-reimbursed cost standard and a frozen plan's FAS service cost of $50m, funded down from a prepayment-credit balance that fell 14% in one year. Removing it entirely and rescaling operating PV (bridge held constant) takes BASE from $343.56 to roughly $270 and the MOS buy-below from $240.49 to roughly $189 — a ~21% cut to the number the board would act on. It does not flip the price verdict (price $532.95 is far above every case), but it materially moves the limit price, which is why this is OPEN_MATERIAL rather than a note. The 4c judge flagged the mechanism in the bear reason only; no anchor adjustment followed.
audit_findings.action: Re-run 4b/4d on two bases: (a) replace CAS pension cost with FAS service cost in each judged year and recompute trend and anchor; (b) keep the recovery but model it as a declining annuity against the $1.9bn prepayment-credit balance rather than as perpetual growing OE. Report both value-per-share and buy-below alongside the current run so the owner sees the spread.

audit_findings.title: $1.7bn of accrued reach-forward losses are future cash outflows charged to neither the numerator nor the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: Accrued in other current liabilities at 6/28/26 (later than the finding's year-end figures): Aeronautics classified $427m (from $495m), MFC classified ~$1,100m (from $1,190m), CMHP $365m — ~$1,892m total, or $8.10/share on 233.535m shares, 2.4% of the $80,232m BASE equity value. Offsetting: the 2025 cash-flow statement shows $1,615m of reach-forward losses as a NON-CASH add-back inside 2025.
audit_findings.mechanism: Two opposing paths. If the $1,615m non-cash charge was added back in the 4b OE build, the anchor is clean of it and the future cash drain sits nowhere — a bridge claim is owed. If it was not added back, the anchor is depressed by ~$1,370m after-tax and the model has already penalised the item — indeed capitalised a one-off charge into perpetuity, which understates value.
audit_findings.evidence: These reach-forward losses do not have an immediate cash flow impact, but as future costs are incurred on these contracts, these losses will negatively impact cash flows over the remaining period of performance.
audit_findings.explanation: The finding's cash logic is right — the expense is behind, the cash is ahead, and the Aeronautics accrual drawing down $68m in six months is direct evidence of the drain. But its conclusion of one-way overstatement does not follow from the record as supplied, because the anchor year is the same year the charges were booked. Which way this cuts turns entirely on one fact I cannot see: whether 4b treated the $1,615m as a non-cash add-back. Materiality is bounded either way — $8.10/share against a $343.56 base and a $189 gap to the current price — so this is a correctness question about the build, not a verdict question. Note also that management states it may record further losses on these programmes that it cannot estimate; that part is a MONITOR item, covered in finding 6.
audit_findings.action: Read the 4b extraction for FY2024 and FY2025 and determine whether the reach-forward loss line ($1,965m 2024, $1,615m 2025) was added back to OE. If added back, add a ~$1.9bn non-debt claim to the bridge and re-run 4d. If not added back, record in PIPELINE.md that the anchor already bears the charge and that no bridge deduction is owed — and consider whether capitalising a one-off charge in perpetuity is itself the larger error.

audit_findings.title: Pension deficit of $3.9bn is undeducted while OE is credited with a 6.50% expected return on assets the shareholder does not own
audit_findings.magnitude: Qualified plans unfunded $3,885m at 12/31/25; accrued pension liabilities $3,931m at 6/28/26. Net of the $666m retiree-medical surplus and the nonqualified plans ($903m gross obligation vs $739m set-aside trust): ~$3,429m, or $14.68/share, 4.3% of the $80,232m BASE equity value. On the numerator leg: expected return $1,439m vs ACTUAL 2025 return of ~10.5% ≈ $2,252m — actual exceeded expected by ~$813m in 2025; 2025 non-service FAS pension was a net EXPENSE of $874m, including a $479m settlement charge.
audit_findings.mechanism: Bridge leg: a senior claim on assets not distributable to shareholders sits outside a bridge that adds $3,791m of cash and deducts nothing for it. Numerator leg: whether expected-return credit reaches OE depends on where the 4b build starts — if OE runs off consolidated operating profit, non-service pension (and the expected return inside it) is excluded; if it runs off net earnings, the anchor carries an $874m expense including a one-off $479m settlement charge.
audit_findings.evidence: We could be required to make pension contributions earlier than and/or in excess of what was planned if our return on pension assets is less than our assumptions, which would reduce our free cash flow.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge question is a real, quantified policy choice the owner should rule on explicitly: ~$3.4bn net, $14.68/share, ~4% of value — not capable of changing the verdict alone, but it compounds with findings 2 and 4 (together ~$9bn, ~$38/share, ~11%). The numerator half of the finding does not survive the filing as written. It asserts OE is 'credited rather than charged'; in 2025 the non-service FAS line was an $874m expense, and the remedy the finding proposes — substituting actual for expected return — would RAISE 2025 income by ~$813m, not lower it, because the plan returned 10.5% against a 6.50% assumption. So the direction is genuinely mixed, and it also matters whether the one-off $479m settlement charge is depressing the anchor.
audit_findings.action: Rule explicitly in PIPELINE.md whether net pension/OPEB deficits are deducted in the OE bridge as a class (this is a doctrine question, not an LMT question), then apply it. Separately, confirm from the 4b extraction whether non-service FAS pension expense — and the $479m 2025 settlement charge — sits inside the anchor; if it does, the anchor is depressed by a non-recurring item and should be examined under the same normalisation test applied to finding 1.

audit_findings.title: The $3.8bn of cash added in the bridge is customer money funding working capital, not surplus
audit_findings.magnitude: Bounded at the full $3,791m added = $16.24/share, 4.7% of the $80,232m BASE equity value and 4.7% of the $343.56 BASE value per share. The audit's unresolved 10-Q WARN can be closed from the filing: at 6/28/26 current maturities of long-term debt were $0 (the $1,168m maturity was repaid in H1 2026), current assets $28,401m vs current liabilities $23,809m — net working capital +$4,592m. Contract liabilities $12,151m (from $11,440m).
audit_findings.mechanism: Bridge: cash and short-term investments added to operating PV as distributable surplus.
audit_findings.evidence: Payments received from customers in advance of revenue recognition are not considered to be significant financing components because they are used to meet working capital demands that can be higher in the early stages of a contract.
audit_findings.explanation: The concern is directionally fair — this is a prepayment-funded business, contract liabilities of $12.2bn dwarf the cash balance, and $3.8bn against $75bn of sales is roughly two weeks of revenue, not a war chest. But the specific ground for a haircut fails on the numbers now checkable in the 10-Q: current maturities are nil, working capital is positive $4.6bn, and the $3,791m in the bridge is the 6/28/26 balance, not a stale year-end figure. Even a 100% haircut moves BASE from $343.56 to $327.32 and buy-below from $240.49 to $229.12 — against a market price of $532.95 the ranking is untouched. Recorded as NOT_MATERIAL on scale, with the caveat that it stacks with findings 2 and 3.
audit_findings.action: No re-run required for this item alone. If findings 2 and 3 trigger a 4d re-run, include a sensitivity that adds only cash in excess of a stated working-capital floor, and record the chosen floor convention in PIPELINE.md so the treatment is consistent across prepayment-funded contractors.

audit_findings.title: Equity-method and portfolio stakes are counted twice — earnings in OE and $1,322m carrying value in the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: Equity-method earnings $28m in 2025 ($56m 2024, $40m 2023); early-stage portfolio net gains $55m pretax ($41m after-tax, $0.18/share). Capitalised at the 10% required return with 2% growth, the two together are worth roughly $0.9bn, ~$3.9/share — 1.1% of the $80,232m BASE equity value — against $1,322m of stakes_net ($653m equity method, mainly ULA; $669m early-stage).
audit_findings.mechanism: Numerator: equity earnings run through other income, net into consolidated operating profit; portfolio marks run through other non-operating income. Bridge: the same assets' carrying values are added as stakes_net. Any component present in both is counted twice.
audit_findings.evidence: Our share of net earnings related to our equity method investees was $ 28 million in 2025, $ 56 million in 2024 and $ 40 million in 2023, of which approximately $ 5 million, $ 45 million and $ 20 million was included in our Space business segment operating profit.
audit_findings.explanation: The mechanism is correctly identified and worth fixing on principle, but the amounts are small on this company: 2025 equity earnings collapsed to $28m from $56m, so the capitalised double-count is roughly a third of one percent of value even before the mark. The $55m of investment marks is the sharper point — a non-recurring valuation gain capitalised in perpetuity — but at $41m after-tax it is 0.7% of the anchor. Separately, and not raised by the finding, the latest 10-Q reports that ULA's Vulcan Centaur is experiencing performance problems that are hurting ULA's financial condition; LMT guaranteed $500m of ULA borrowings in Q2 2026, recognised a $64m guarantee liability, and states it expects to provide further support and could incur impairment. That puts the durability of the $653m equity-method carrying value itself in question — see finding 6.
audit_findings.action: Check the 4b extraction for whether other income, net (including the $28m equity earnings) and the $55m of non-operating investment marks were purged from each judged year. Apply the rule once, consistently: purge the income OR drop the corresponding carrying value from stakes_net, never neither and never both. Given the scale, fix in the next scheduled refresh rather than re-running 4d now.

audit_findings.title: Contingent programme and offset exposures sit outside both the numerator and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: CMHP contract assets $585m at 6/28/26 (down from $625m at year-end) = $2.50/share, 0.7% of BASE equity value; cumulative CMHP losses ~$670m with $365m still accrued. Offsets: $19.9bn notional to 2044 with ~$2.2bn of estimated penalties. Letters of credit and surety bonds $3.3bn at 6/28/26 (from $3.5bn). ULA borrowing guarantee: $500m maximum potential future payments, $64m liability recognised. TUHP: the ~$115m contingency is NOT still open — the 10-Q states all required export licences are now in place and 'the risk of customer drawdown on letters of credit linked to obtaining these licenses has been eliminated.'
audit_findings.mechanism: None of these are presently in the numerator or the bridge. They would enter as future non-debt claims on cash if they crystallise, or as write-downs of contract assets already on the balance sheet.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, cumulative losses recognized on the program remained at approximately $ 670 million and approximately $ 625 million of contract assets remained on the balance sheet.
audit_findings.explanation: Correctly characterised as outside the model, but these are contingencies, not present claims, so MONITOR is the right shelf rather than a bridge deduction. Two of the finding's specifics have moved since the anchor 10-K and the finding did not catch it: the TUHP licence contingency is closed per the latest 10-Q, and the CMHP contract asset has drawn down to $585m. The offset penalties are notional-linked and management states it has historically not been required to pay material penalties; treating $2.2bn as an expected claim would be a large unsupported haircut. Even the hardest concrete exposure — full write-off of the $585m CMHP contract asset — is 0.7% of value. The item that has genuinely deteriorated since the anchor year is ULA, which is a stakes_net question (finding 5) as well as a contingency: $500m guaranteed, further support expected, impairment flagged by management.
audit_findings.action: Add to the quality layer as a watch list with named triggers: (1) outcome of the Canadian government restructuring talks and any further CMHP contract-asset movement; (2) ULA Vulcan performance, any additional LMT financial support beyond the $500m guarantee, and any impairment of the $617m carrying value; (3) any drawdown on the $3.3bn of letters of credit and surety bonds. Re-read the next 10-Q against these three. No bridge change now.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed/computed: FY2016 residual $48.0m, 4.0% of filed D&A (other years not supplied). Applying the same 4.0% to 2025's filed $1,687m composite D&A gives ~$67m pretax, ~$57m after-tax at the 15.3% 2025 effective rate — 1.0% of the $5,650.9m anchor.
audit_findings.mechanism: Numerator: eligible D&A add-backs are identified line by line; anything unidentified stays as an expense, so OE is stated at or below its true level. It cannot inflate the anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2016 $48.0m (4.0% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: This is a disclosed conservatism, not a defect, and it is one-directional: it can only understate value. At roughly 1% of the anchor on the one year quantified, it is immaterial by construction. It also cannot change the anchor rule — 4d took MIN(trend, latest) and the trend ($6,945m) already sat above the latest actual, so raising OE across all years by ~1% leaves the anchor at the latest actual and the value effect proportional and trivial. Recorded so the owner knows the bias direction, not because it requires work.
audit_findings.action: None required. If the residual is ever classified, do it as part of a scheduled 4b methodology change across all names rather than as an LMT-specific re-run, and only if filed evidence identifies the components as eligible non-economic add-backs.
